b: Not promises but observations about how life generally works: about money, speech, work, sex, anger and friendship. Read as guarantees they will disappoint; read as the grain of the universe they are extremely useful.
Thirty-one chapters, which makes one a day for a month a natural habit.

1.t: The fear of the LORD is the starting point rather than the conclusion — everything in the book assumes it.
Personified as a woman shouting in public. The rebuke is that people ignore what is freely available.

3.h: Lean not on your own understanding
3.t: Trust with the whole heart, acknowledge him, and he makes the paths straight. Frequently quoted as a promise about outcomes; it is about direction.

3.h: Honour the LORD with your wealth
3.t: Firstfruits rather than leftovers. The proverb assumes giving comes off the top.

3.h: Do not despise the LORD's discipline
3.t: Quoted in Hebrews 12. He disciplines those he loves, as a father the son he delights in.

8.t: A poetic figure, presented as a woman, who was beside God at creation. Reading her as a created being who made the world is a great deal of weight for a figure of speech to carry. Worth talking through with a pastor or a mature Christian you trust.

31.t: An acrostic poem. She trades, buys land, plants a vineyard and speaks with wisdom. Not a checklist so much as a portrait of strength.

4.t: Above all else, because everything you do flows from it. The chapter is a father's instruction to a son.

6.t: Practical wisdom about work, followed by the sluggard's slow slide into poverty.
A list God hates, and six of the seven concern how people treat one another with words.

10.t: From here the book is mostly two-line sayings setting the wise against the foolish. Read a few at a time rather than in bulk.

13.t: The companion of fools suffers harm. As blunt a statement about friendship as Scripture gives.

15.t: Turns away wrath. The chapter has a dozen sayings about speech and most of them are about restraint.

16.t: But the LORD establishes his steps. Verse 18 — pride before destruction — is from the same chapter.

18.t: Is folly and shame. Verse 17 makes the same point: the first to present his case seems right until another comes and questions him.

22.t: A proverb rather than a guarantee, which matters enormously to parents whose children have walked away.

27.t: Are faithful; an enemy's kisses are profuse. Verse 17 — iron sharpens iron — is a reason for friends to ask each other hard questions.

11.t: Where there is no guidance a people falls. Repeated at 15:22 and 24:6 — Proverbs rarely says anything three times by accident.

12.h: A fool is right in his own eyes
12.t: But the wise listen to advice. Probably the single most repeated idea in the book.

14.t: There is a way that appears right to a man, and its end is death. Stated twice, here and at 16:25.

17.h: A friend loves at all times
17.t: And a brother is born for a time of adversity.

19.t: But the LORD's purpose prevails. Sovereignty stated in one line of Hebrew poetry.

20.t: Proverbs is repeatedly blunt about drink, without being prohibitionist.
The purposes of a man's heart are deep waters, but one who has insight draws them out. A description of what good listening does.

24.h: Though the righteous fall seven times
24.t: They rise again. Failure is assumed rather than excluded.

28.t: Does not prosper, but the one who confesses and renounces them finds mercy. The Proverbs version of 1 John 1:9.

29.h: Fear of man is a snare
29.t: But whoever trusts in the LORD is kept safe. A verse about the actual reason most men stay quiet.

2.h: If you search for it as for silver
2.t: Wisdom requires effort and seeking — and then verse 6 says the LORD gives it. Both are true.

5.h: Drink water from your own cistern
5.t: A frank warning against adultery and a celebration of faithfulness within marriage.

7.t: A story told from a window: a youth walking toward a house he should avoid, at dusk. The warning is about drifting, not deciding.

9.t: Wisdom and Folly both set a table and call out to the passers-by. The reader has to choose which house to enter.

21.t: Is a stream of water in the LORD's hand. Even rulers are within his direction.

23.t: The clearest description of drunkenness in Scripture, ending with the drunk man wanting another drink.

25.t: Give him food. Paul quotes this in Romans 12 as the way to overcome evil with good.

26.h: Answer a fool — and do not
26.t: Two contradictory proverbs placed side by side on purpose. Wisdom knows which situation calls for which.

30.t: Agur's prayer: give me only my daily bread, lest I become proud or desperate.
